**G1 finding.** The specs and code say only that a refused payload is kept and redelivered. A waiting entry gets none of the four delivery checks the triage names.

SIL-B19 is at `self-improvement.spec.md` l.162-166. SIL-AC10 (l.204) is the criterion that names it, together with SIL-B20 and SIL-B6. `improvement-proposals.spec.md` l.152 (PRP-B25) and l.208 (PRP-B29) also wait on this outbox.

I did not re-read `filing.py`, `release.py` or the tests this turn. Those claims are carried over from the earlier attempt, apart from the `filing.py` l.340, 363, 446 and 505 hits that a search just confirmed.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: SIL-B19 (`self-improvement.spec.md` l.162-166) says only that on a refusal or unreachable host the payload is kept in `filing-outbox.jsonl` and redelivered with the next filing. SIL-AC10 (l.204; names SIL-B19, SIL-B20, SIL-B6) is the criterion that proves it, and SIL-AC3 (l.196) is about a repeated cause. PRP-B25 (`improvement-proposals.spec.md` l.152) and PRP-B29 (l.208) also wait on this outbox. No spec states a check against open issues, a comment instead of create, a mute drop or an age limit. `max_age` appears in no file under `plugins/tempergraph/docs` except the triage note (l.32), so `outbox.max_age_days` has no parameter record. `mute.days` is the model: 30, loop-issues ISS-B3, its ADR `a-closed-loop-issue-mutes-its-fingerprint-or-links-a-regression.adr.md`, and the `improvement-data` parameter rule IMD-AC3. Code, `improve/filing.py` (basis `read`; plain keep and redeliver `tested`): `Outbox` l.340-360 is a JSONL file with `add` and `take`. `take` reads all, unlinks and returns all, with no age or order logic. Entries hold op (`comment`, `create` or `reopen`), repo, number or title/body/labels, and fingerprint. No timestamp is stored, so age cannot be computed today. `_deliver` l.363-369 posts an entry with no search, mute or age check. `file()` l.443-448 redelivers every taken entry first, unless it is a dry run. On `CodeHostError` the entry is re-added. Otherwise `{op: redelivered, url, fingerprint}` is recorded (l.446). The open-issue match (`_match_open` l.396) and the mute check (l.472-487) run only for new decisions, so a queued create can duplicate an issue filed since. Fresh failures record `{op: queued}` (l.505). Other writers: `release.py` `_reopen` l.44-59, and `cli/improve.py` l.371 (the PRP-B25 trial comment). `improve/trials.py` l.492 also records `{op: queued}`. Tests: `test_filing.py` l.188 `test_dedup_retry_dry_run_and_outbox` and `test_loop_issues.py` l.467 assert plain keep and redeliver only. `central-run-stats` CST-B12 and TEL-B36/37 are the stats outbox, a different one. The open-issue match rules are ISS-B7, and the cap on "seen again" comments (ISS-B13) applies to new decisions only.
